title: ORDER BY on a boolean column puts BLANK before FALSE
query: EVALUATE Flags ORDER BY Flags[F], Flags[Id]

source.supports: ASC is the default and sorts ascending; the page does not say where BLANK goes

source.quote: This sometimes proves useful for sorting purposes because TRUE > FALSE

derivation: Flags[F] by Id: TRUE (1), FALSE (2), BLANK (3), TRUE (4). FALSE sorts before TRUE. BLANK is taken as the lowest value, before FALSE: Ids 3, 2, 1, 4.
alternative: No source states where BLANK sorts among booleans. If ORDER BY treats BLANK as equal to FALSE (as = does), the tie falls to Flags[Id] and the order is Ids 2, 3, 1, 4.
notes: FALSE has the lower Id on purpose, so the two readings give different orders.
